TOPICS: safety guidelines, heat hazards, power adapter safety, battery safety, handling and carrying, electrical safety, ventilation, hearing protection, choking hazards, disposal

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- Read the important safety information first. (Page 7)
- The information in this document does not alter the terms of your purchase agreement or the Lenovo Limited Warranty. (Page 7)
- Power adapters and other features can create potential safety risks that can result in physical injury or property damage, especially if misused. (Page 7)
- When your computer is turned on or the battery is charging, the base, the palm rest, and some other parts may become hot. (Page 7)
- Extended contact with your body, even through clothing, could cause discomfort or even a skin burn. (Page 7)
- The AC power adapter generates heat when connected to an electrical outlet and computer, which can cause skin burns with extended contact. (Page 8)
- Do not place the AC power adapter in contact with any part of your body while in use, and never use it to warm your body. (Page 8)
- Keep liquids away from the computer to avoid spills and electrical shock. (Page 8)
- Applying strong force to cables may damage or break them; communication lines should be routed to avoid being walked on, tripped over, or pinched. (Page 8)
- Before moving a computer equipped with a hard disk drive, turn it off, put it in sleep mode, or put it in hibernation mode to prevent damage and data loss. (Page 8)
- Handle your computer gently and carry your computer carefully. (Page 9)
- Specific actions to avoid include dropping, bumping, scratching, twisting, hitting, vibrating, pushing, or placing heavy objects on the computer, display, or external devices. (Page 9)
- Users must use a quality carrying case with adequate cushioning and protection. (Page 9)
- Computers should not be packed in tightly packed suitcases or bags. (Page 9)
- Before placing a computer in a carrying case, it must be turned off, in sleep mode, or in hibernation mode; computers should never be placed in a case while turned on. (Page 9)
- Conditions requiring immediate action include odors, puffs of smoke, sparks, popping, cracking, or hissing sounds. (Page 9)
- Users should not attempt to diagnose issues themselves and must contact the Customer Support Center. (Page 9)
- The web address https://pcsupport.lenovo.com/supportphonelist is provided for Service and Support phone numbers. (Page 9)
- Products with cracked, broken, or damaged plugs, power adapters, extension cords, surge protectors, or power supplies should not be used. (Page 10)
- Signs of overheating, smoke, sparks, fire, battery damage, unusual sounds, liquid spills, water exposure, drops, or abnormal operation indicate a potential hazard. (Page 10)
- Non-Lenovo products (e.g., extension cords) must be discontinued until the manufacturer is contacted or a replacement is obtained. (Page 10)
- Customers should not service a product themselves; only approved Service Providers can perform repairs. (Page 10)
- Upgrades are called "options," and replaceable parts are "Customer Replaceable Units (CRUs)." (Page 10)
- Before removing covers, ensure the power is off and the product is unplugged. (Page 10)
- A caution warns of hazardous moving parts and to keep fingers away. (Page 10)
- Another caution states to turn off the computer and wait several minutes for it to cool before opening the cover. (Page 10)
- Use only power adapters supplied by the product manufacturer. (Page 11)
- Never wrap a power adapter cable around a power adapter or other object. (Page 11)
- Protect power adapters from liquids (e.g., sinks, tubs, toilets, liquid cleansers). (Page 11)
- Do not use any power adapter that shows corrosion at the ac input pins or signs of overheating (deformed plastic). (Page 11)
- Ensure all power adapter connectors are securely and completely plugged into receptacles. (Page 11)
- Extension cords, surge protectors, uninterruptible power supplies, and power strips must be rated to handle the product's electrical requirements. (Page 11)
- Never overload these devices; load should not exceed the power strip input rating. (Page 11)
- Do not use a damaged or corroded power outlet; have it replaced by a qualified electrician. (Page 12)
- Do not bend or modify the plug; contact the manufacturer for a replacement if damaged. (Page 12)
- Do not share an outlet with appliances that draw large amounts of electricity to prevent unstable voltage. (Page 12)
- Some products have a three-pronged plug that fits only into a grounded outlet; do not defeat this safety feature. (Page 12)
- Never overload an electrical outlet; the overall system load should not exceed 80 percent of the branch circuit rating. (Page 12)
- Do not fully extend power adapter cables in a way that will stress the cords. (Page 12)
- Never remove the cover on a power supply or any part with the specified hazard label attached. (Page 12)
- Hazardous voltage, current, and energy levels are present inside components with the label. (Page 12)
- There are no serviceable parts inside these components; contact a service technician if a problem is suspected. (Page 12)
- Do not connect or disconnect external device cables other than USB and 1394 while the computer power is on. (Page 13)
- Wait at least five seconds after the computer is shut down to disconnect external devices. (Page 13)
- Batteries supplied by Lenovo have been tested for compatibility and should only be replaced with approved parts. (Page 13)
- A battery other than the one specified by Lenovo, or a disassembled or modified battery is not covered by the warranty. (Page 13)
- Battery abuse can cause overheat, liquid leakage, or an explosion. (Page 13)
- Store rechargeable batteries charged to approximately 30 to 50% of capacity. (Page 13)
- Recharge batteries about once per year to prevent overdischarge. (Page 13)
- Do not dispose of batteries in landfills; comply with local ordinances. (Page 13)
- Only recharge the battery strictly according to instructions in the product documentation. (Page 13)
- Incorrect battery replacement poses a danger of explosion. (Page 13)
- The battery contains a small amount of harmful substances. (Page 13)
- Do not attempt to remove or replace the built-in rechargeable battery; replacement must be done by a Lenovo-authorized repair facility or technician. (Page 14)
- Only recharge the battery strictly according to instructions included in the product documentation. (Page 14)
- The battery contains a small amount of harmful substance and should not be heated to more than $100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (212°F). (Page 14)
- Products containing manganese dioxide lithium coin-cell batteries may contain perchlorate, which requires special handling. (Page 14)
- Users in California are directed to https://www.dtsc.ca.gov/hazardouswaste/perchlorate/ for more information. (Page 14)
- Computers, AC power adapters, and accessories can generate heat when turned on or charging. (Page 15)
- Notebook computers can generate a significant amount of heat due to their compact size. (Page 15)
- Avoid keeping hands, lap, or body parts in contact with hot sections of the computer. (Page 15)
- Do not operate the computer or charge the battery near flammable materials or in explosive environments. (Page 15)
- Ventilation slots, fans, and heat sinks must not be blocked by placing the product on soft surfaces like beds or sofas. (Page 15)
- Do not place the AC power adapter in contact with any part of the body while using it. (Page 15)
- Airflow temperatures into the computer should not exceed 35°C (95°F). (Page 15)
- Electric current from power, telephone, and communication cables is hazardous. (Page 16)
- To avoid shock hazard: Do not use computer during lightning storm, do not connect/disconnect cables during an electrical storm, connect power adapter to properly wired and grounded outlet, use one hand only when possible, never turn on equipment if fire/water/structural damage is present, disconnect power adapter and all cables before opening device covers, and do not use computer until internal parts are fastened. (Page 16)
- Procedures for connecting: Turn everything OFF, attach all cables to devices, attach signal cables, attach power adapter to outlets, turn devices ON. (Page 16)
- Procedures for disconnecting: Turn everything OFF, remove power adapter from outlets, remove signal cables, remove all cables from devices. (Page 16)
- The power adapter must be disconnected before installing other electrical cables and can only be reconnected after all other cables are connected. (Page 16)
- Liquid crystal display (LCD) is made of glass and can break if dropped; if internal fluid contacts eyes or hands, wash affected areas with water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical care if symptoms persist. (Page 16)
- Excessive sound pressure from headphones can cause hearing loss. (Page 17)
- The computer's headphone output complies with EN 50332-2 Sub clause 7, limiting maximum wide band true RMS output voltage to 150 mV. (Page 17)
- Headphones or earphones must comply with EN 50332-2 (Clause 7 limits) for a wide band characteristic voltage of 75 mV. (Page 17)
- If Lenovo computer came with headphones, the combination complies with EN 50332-1. (Page 17)
- Using non-compliant headphones can be dangerous due to excessive sound pressure levels. (Page 17)
- Choking hazard notice: Product contains small parts; keep away from children under three years. (Page 17)
- Plastic bag notice: Keep plastic bags away from babies and children to avoid danger of suffocation. (Page 17)
- Glass parts notice: Some parts may be made of glass; do not touch broken glass; stop using the product until replaced by trained personnel. (Page 17)
- Note: Products with mercury-containing fluorescent lamps require disposal according to local, state, or federal laws. (Page 17)

Follow and retain all information included with your computer. The information in this document does not alter the terms of your purchase agreement or the Lenovo Limited Warranty. For more information, see "Warranty Information" in the Safety and Warranty Guide that comes with your computer. Customer safety is important. Our products are developed to be safe and effective. However, personal computers are electronic devices. Power adapters and other features can create potential safety risks that can result in physical injury or property damage, especially if misused. To reduce these risks, follow the instructions included with your product, observe all warnings on the product and in the operating instructions, and review the information included in this document carefully. By carefully following the information contained in this document and provided with your product, you can help protect yourself from hazards and create a safer computer work environment. Note: This information includes references to power adapters and batteries. In addition to notebook computers, some products (such as speakers and monitors) ship with external power adapters. If you have such a product, this information applies to your product. In addition, computer products contain a coin-sized internal battery that provides power to the system clock even when the computer is unplugged, so the battery safety information applies to all computer products. Important information about using your computer Ensure that you follow the important tips given here to get the most use and enjoyment out of your computer. Failure to do so might lead to discomfort or injury, or cause the computer to fail. Protect yourself from the heat that your computer generates. When your computer is turned on or the battery is charging, the base, the palm rest, and some other parts may become hot. The temperature they reach depends on the amount of system activity and the level of charge in the battery. Extended contact with your body, even through clothing, could cause discomfort or even a skin burn.

sections.summary:
<section_card>
SECTION: Important safety information (Pages 7-19)

TOPICS: safety guidelines, heat hazards, power adapter safety, battery safety, handling and carrying, electrical safety, ventilation, hearing protection, choking hazards, disposal

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- Read the important safety information first. (Page 7)
- The information in this document does not alter the terms of your purchase agreement or the Lenovo Limited Warranty. (Page 7)
- Power adapters and other features can create potential safety risks that can result in physical injury or property damage, especially if misused. (Page 7)
- When your computer is turned on or the battery is charging, the base, the palm rest, and some other parts may become hot. (Page 7)
- Extended contact with your body, even through clothing, could cause discomfort or even a skin burn. (Page 7)
- The AC power adapter generates heat when connected to an electrical outlet and computer, which can cause skin burns with extended contact. (Page 8)
- Do not place the AC power adapter in contact with any part of your body while in use, and never use it to warm your body. (Page 8)
- Keep liquids away from the computer to avoid spills and electrical shock. (Page 8)
- Applying strong force to cables may damage or break them; communication lines should be routed to avoid being walked on, tripped over, or pinched. (Page 8)
- Before moving a computer equipped with a hard disk drive, turn it off, put it in sleep mode, or put it in hibernation mode to prevent damage and data loss. (Page 8)
- Handle your computer gently and carry your computer carefully. (Page 9)
- Specific actions to avoid include dropping, bumping, scratching, twisting, hitting, vibrating, pushing, or placing heavy objects on the computer, display, or external devices. (Page 9)
- Users must use a quality carrying case with adequate cushioning and protection. (Page 9)
- Computers should not be packed in tightly packed suitcases or bags. (Page 9)
- Before placing a computer in a carrying case, it must be turned off, in sleep mode, or in hibernation mode; computers should never be placed in a case while turned on. (Page 9)
- Conditions requiring immediate action include odors, puffs of smoke, sparks, popping, cracking, or hissing sounds. (Page 9)
- Users should not attempt to diagnose issues themselves and must contact the Customer Support Center. (Page 9)
- The web address https://pcsupport.lenovo.com/supportphonelist is provided for Service and Support phone numbers. (Page 9)
- Products with cracked, broken, or damaged plugs, power adapters, extension cords, surge protectors, or power supplies should not be used. (Page 10)
- Signs of overheating, smoke, sparks, fire, battery damage, unusual sounds, liquid spills, water exposure, drops, or abnormal operation indicate a potential hazard. (Page 10)
- Non-Lenovo products (e.g., extension cords) must be discontinued until the manufacturer is contacted or a replacement is obtained. (Page 10)
- Customers should not service a product themselves; only approved Service Providers can perform repairs. (Page 10)
- Upgrades are called "options," and replaceable parts are "Customer Replaceable Units (CRUs)." (Page 10)
- Before removing covers, ensure the power is off and the product is unplugged. (Page 10)
- A caution warns of hazardous moving parts and to keep fingers away. (Page 10)
- Another caution states to turn off the computer and wait several minutes for it to cool before opening the cover. (Page 10)
- Use only power adapters supplied by the product manufacturer. (Page 11)
- Never wrap a power adapter cable around a power adapter or other object. (Page 11)
- Protect power adapters from liquids (e.g., sinks, tubs, toilets, liquid cleansers). (Page 11)
- Do not use any power adapter that shows corrosion at the ac input pins or signs of overheating (deformed plastic). (Page 11)
- Ensure all power adapter connectors are securely and completely plugged into receptacles. (Page 11)
- Extension cords, surge protectors, uninterruptible power supplies, and power strips must be rated to handle the product's electrical requirements. (Page 11)
- Never overload these devices; load should not exceed the power strip input rating. (Page 11)
- Do not use a damaged or corroded power outlet; have it replaced by a qualified electrician. (Page 12)
- Do not bend or modify the plug; contact the manufacturer for a replacement if damaged. (Page 12)
- Do not share an outlet with appliances that draw large amounts of electricity to prevent unstable voltage. (Page 12)
- Some products have a three-pronged plug that fits only into a grounded outlet; do not defeat this safety feature. (Page 12)

pages.ocr_text: Power adapters DANGER Use only the power adapters supplied by the product manufacturer. Never wrap a power adapter cable around a power adapter or other object. Doing so can stress the cord in ways that can cause the power adapter cable to fray, crack, or crimp. This can present a safety hazard. Always route the power adapter cable so that they will not be walked on, tripped over, or pinched by objects. Protect power adapters from liquids. For instance, do not leave your power adapter near sinks, tubs, toilets, or on floors that are cleaned with liquid cleansers. Liquids can cause a short circuit, particularly if the power adapter has been stressed by misuse. Liquids also can cause gradual corrosion of the connector terminals on a power adapter, which can eventually result in overheating. Ensure that all power adapter connectors are securely and completely plugged into receptacles. This chapter provides information to help you use the various features provided by your computer.
Registering your computer

When you register your computer, information is entered into a database, which enables Lenovo to contact you if there is a recall or other severe problem. In addition, some locations offer extended privileges and services to registered users.
When you register your computer with Lenovo, you also will receive the following benefits:
To register your computer with Lenovo, go to https://support.lenovo.com/productregistration and follow the instructions on the screen.
Frequently asked questions
This topic provides a few tips to help you optimize the use of your ThinkPad notebook computers.
Can I get my user guide in another language?
To download the user guide in another language, go to https://support.lenovo.com. Then follow the instructions on the screen.
How do I get help about the Windows operating system?

The Windows help information system provides you with detailed information about using the Windows operating system so that you can get the most of your computer. To access the Windows help information system, click the Start button to open the Start menu, and then click Get Help. Additionally, you can use the Cortana® personal assistant to search for help, apps, files, settings, and so on.
How do I access Control Panel?
Click the Start button to open the Start menu, and then click Windows System  $\rightarrow$  Control Panel.
How to turn off my computer?
Open the Start menu, click Power, and then click Shut down.
How to partition my storage drive?
To partition the storage drive of your computer in the Windows operating system, refer to https:// support.lenovo.com/solutions/ht503851.
How do I use battery power more effectively when I am on the go?

<section_card>
SECTION: Chapter 2. Using your computer (Pages 35-57)

TOPICS: Computer registration, frequently asked questions, touch gestures, multi-touch screen, keyboard and function keys, pointing devices, battery management, power settings, network connections, NFC, audio features, cameras, media cards, external displays, travel tips

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- Registering a computer with Lenovo allows users to be contacted about recalls and provides benefits including quicker service, automatic notifications for free software, and special promotional offers (Page 35)
- The registration URL is https://support.lenovo.com/productregistration (Page 35)
- FAQ section covers accessing Windows help, Control Panel, shutting down the computer, partitioning storage, and using battery power effectively (Page 35)
- Instructions for accessing Windows help via Start menu and Cortana® (Page 35)
- Instructions for accessing Control Panel: Start → Windows System → Control Panel (Page 35)
- Instructions for shutting down: Start menu → Power → Shut down (Page 35)
- Link for partitioning storage drive: https://support.lenovo.com/solutions/ht503851 (Page 35)
- Tips for effective battery use are found on page 28 under "Power-saving modes" and "Managing the battery power" (Page 35)
- Secure data disposal requires reading "Deleting data from your storage drive" on page 58 after studying Chapter 5 "Security" on page 53 (Page 36)
- Attaching an external display is covered in "Using an external display" on page 36 (Page 36)
- Device attachment or replacement is detailed in Chapter 9 "Replacing devices" on page 99 (Page 36)
- For a slow computer, follow "General tips for preventing problems" on page 79 and use diagnostic software mentioned on the same page (Page 36)
- Recommended printed topics include "Installing the Windows 10 operating system" (page 61), "Computer stops responding" (page 80), and "Power problems" (page 92) (Page 36)
- Touch gestures are for touch models only and include tap, tap and hold, slide, drag, zoom out, zoom in, swipe from right edge, swipe from left edge, and swiping from top edge (Page 37)
- Short swipe from top edge shows hidden title bar; long swipe closes current app in tablet mode (Page 37)
- Multi-touch screen is a glass panel covered with plastic film that can be damaged by pressure or metallic objects (Page 38)
- Do not use fingernails, gloved fingers, or inanimate objects for input on the screen (Page 38)
- Cleaning requires turning off the computer, using a dry, soft, lint-free cloth or absorbent cotton, and gently wiping with a top-down motion without applying pressure (Page 38)
- Special keys include Fn key, Ctrl key, and Windows key (Page 38)
- Pressing the Windows logo key opens the Start menu (Page 39)
- Fn key and function keys can be configured in the Keyboard Properties window (Page 39)
- Users can change the view of Control Panel from Category to Large icons or Small icons (Page 39)
- Lenovo - Keyboard Manager window accessed by clicking "Lenovo - Keyboard Manager" (Page 39)
- Key combinations with F12 (Shift+F12, Alt+F12, Ctrl+F12) can have different functions defined (Page 39)
- Snipping Tool program opened with Fn + PrtSc key combination (Page 39)
- ThinkPad pointing device enables all traditional mouse functions: pointing, clicking, scrolling, and touch gestures like rotating and zooming (Page 40)
- Components are TrackPoint pointing device and trackpad (Page 40)
- Both TrackPoint and trackpad are active by default with touch gestures enabled (Page 40)
- To change settings, see "Customizing the ThinkPad pointing device" on page 25 (Page 40)
- TrackPoint consists of pointing stick (1), left-click button (2), right-click button (3), scroll bar (4) (Page 41)
- Pointing: apply pressure to pointing-stick nonslip cap (1) in any direction parallel to the keyboard (Page 41)
- Left-click: press left-click button (2) (Page 41)
- Right-click: press right-click button (3) (Page 41)
- Scrolling: press and hold dotted scroll bar (4) while applying pressure to pointing stick (Page 41)
- Trackpad surface is sensitive to finger touch and movement (Page 42)
- Trackpad divided into left-click zone (primary-click zone) and right-click zone (secondary-click zone) (Page 42)
- Left-click: press left-click zone or tap anywhere on trackpad with one finger (Page 42)
- Right-click: press right-click zone or tap with two fingers (Page 42)
- Scrolling: use two fingers on trackpad and move them vertically or horizontally (Page 42)
- For more information on touch gestures, see "Using the trackpad touch gestures" on page 25 (Page 42)
- If trackpad is stained with oil, turn off computer and wipe with soft, lint-free cloth moistened with lukewarm water or computer cleaner (Page 42)
- Trackpad touch gestures include tapping with one or two fingers, scrolling, zooming, swiping with three fingers (Page 43)
- Tap with one finger selects or opens item; two-finger tap displays shortcut menu (Page 43)
- Two-finger scroll enables vertical or horizontal scrolling (Page 43)
- Two-finger zoom in/out performed by moving fingers apart or closer together (Page 43)
- Swipe three fingers up opens task view to see all open windows (Page 43)
- Swipe three fingers down shows desktop (Page 43)
- Customization options include enabling/disabling TrackPoint, trackpad, and touch gestures (Page 43)
- To customize, go to Control Panel, click Mouse, and follow instructions in Mouse Properties window (Page 43)
- Cap on pointing stick is removable and may need replacement after extended use (Page 44)
- Use cap with grooves as shown in illustration (Page 44)
- Computer includes USB-C type AC power adapter and power cord (Page 44)
- Connecting AC power adapter: connect power cord to adapter, connect adapter to USB-C port, plug power cord into electrical outlet (Page 44)
- Using improper power cord might severely damage computer (Page 44)
- Tips: disconnect adapter when not in use, avoid tight binding of power cord around transformer pack (Page 44)
- Battery-status icon in Windows notification area shows remaining power percentage and estimated usage time (Page 45)
- Rate of battery consumption depends on user habits, including storage drive access frequency, display brightness, wireless feature usage (Page 45)
- Full charge takes about four to eight hours, depending on battery size, environment, and computer use (Page 45)
- Recharging does not start if battery level above 95% to maximize lifespan (Page 45)
- Optimal charging temperature range: 10°C (50°F) to 35°C (95°F) (Page 45)
- Charging should occur when new battery installed, power level low, or battery unused for long time (Page 45)
- To maximize battery life: use battery until depleted, recharge fully before use, always use power management features (Page 46)
- Adjust power plan settings: Control Panel → Large/Small icons → Power Options → follow on-screen instructions (Page 46)
- Sleep mode: work saved to memory, storage drive and display turned off; wakes up within seconds (Page 46)
- Hibernation mode: all open programs, folders, files saved to storage drive, computer powers off completely (Page 46)
- Wake-up function for hibernation disabled by default; enable via System and Security > Administrative Tools > Task Scheduler > Conditions tab > Power > Wake the computer to run this task (Page 46)
- Wake-up function consumes no power when disabled, small amount when enabled (Page 46)
- Turn off wireless features like Bluetooth or wireless LAN when not in use to conserve power (Page 47)
- Ethernet connector has green indicator for LAN connection, yellow for data transmission (Page 47)
- DANGER warning: do not connect telephone cable to Ethernet connector to avoid electrical shock (Page 47)
- Establish wireless-LAN connection: press F8, click wireless-network-connection-status icon, double-click network (Page 47)
- Computer automatically connects to available remembered wireless networks when location changes (Page 47)
- Tips for best signal: minimize obstacles between computer and access point, open computer cover at angle >90 degrees (Page 47)
- Check connection status via wireless-network-connection-status icon in Windows notification area (Page 47)
- Wireless-WAN uses cellular networks (HSPA, 3G, 4G, LTE) for remote connectivity (Page 48)
- Tips for best wireless-WAN connection: keep computer away from body, place on flat surface at angle >90 degrees, avoid concrete/brick walls (Page 48)
- Wireless-network-connection-status icon shows signal strength with more bars indicating better signal (Page 48)
- Bluetooth used for connecting peripherals, transferring data, remote control of mobile phones (Page 48)
- Warning: do not use 802.11 wireless feature simultaneously with Bluetooth to prevent performance degradation (Page 48)
- Enable Bluetooth: press Bluetooth-control key (F10) or navigate through Windows Settings → Devices → Bluetooth & other devices (Page 48)
- NFC is high-frequency, short-range wireless communication technology (Page 49)
- NFC feature enabled by default but can be disabled; requires turning off Airplane mode then enabling NFC (Page 49)
- Pair with NFC card: ensure card in NDEF format, position within 0.5 cm (0.20 inches) of NFC label (Page 49)
- Align shorter edge of card with horizontal extension line of NFC label, hold until detection confirmed (Page 49)
- Pairing smartphone with NFC: position within 5 cm (1.97 inches) of NFC label (Page 50)
- Airplane mode disables all wireless features; toggle via Settings → Network & Internet → Airplane mode (Page 50)
- Computer has 3.5 mm (0.14 inches) audio connector, microphones, speakers (Page 50)
- Supported audio functions: High Definition Audio, MIDI/MP3 playback, PCM/WAV recording, multi-source recording (Page 50)
- Headset with 3.5-mm 4-pole plug supports headphone and microphone functions (Page 50)
- Conventional microphone not supported (Page 50)
- Smart audio feature limits maximum wide band true RMS output voltage to 130 mV when headset connected (Page 51)
- Change setting: Control Panel → SmartAudio → Disable Headphone Limiter (Page 51)
- Conventional camera requires sliding Think Shutter to left to unveil lens (Page 51)
- Infrared camera enables face authentication for signing in (Page 51)
- Camera settings configurable through Lenovo Vantage → Hardware Settings → Audio/Visual (Page 51)
- Infrared camera indicator on means recognition mode (Page 52)
- Set up face authentication: Settings → Accounts → Sign-in options → create password/PIN → set up Face Recognition under Windows Hello (Page 52)
- Unlock computer: select smiling face icon on lock screen and follow instructions (Page 52)
- Supports MMC, SD, SDXC, SDHC media cards (Page 52)
- Does not support CPRM for SD cards (Page 52)
- Smart cards used for authentication, data storage, application processing, single sign-on (SSO) (Page 52)
- Smart-card reader supports cards with dimensions: Length: 85.60 mm (3.37 inches), Width: 53.98 mm (2.13 inches), Thickness: 0.76 mm (0.03 inches) (Page 52)
- Smart cards with slits not supported and can damage reader (Page 53)
- Touch grounded metal object to reduce static electricity before handling cards (Page 53)
- Installation steps: locate correct slot, orient card properly (metal contacts down for media cards, up for smart cards), press firmly into slot (Page 53)
- Enable plug-and-play: Control Panel > Hardware and Sound > Device Manager > Add legacy hardware (Page 53)
- Removal: stop card first, avoid sleep/hibernation during data transfer, use "Safely Remove Hardware and Eject Media" icon in Windows (Page 53)
- Supports up to 4096 x 2304 pixels / 60 Hz with USB-C or USB-C (Thunderbolt 3 compatible) connector (Page 54)

pages.ocr_text: Using the battery When you use your computer away from electrical outlets, you depend on battery power to keep your computer running. Different computer components consume power at different rates. The more you use the power-intensive components, the faster you consume battery power. Spend more time unplugged with ThinkPad batteries. Mobility has revolutionized business by enabling you to take your work wherever you go. With ThinkPad batteries, you are able to work longer without being tied to an electrical outlet. Checking the battery status Move your pointer to the battery-status icon in the Windows notification area to check the battery status. The battery-status icon displays the percentage of battery power remaining and how long you can use your computer before you must charge the battery. The rate at which you use battery power determines how long you can use the battery of your computer between charges. Because every computer user has individual habits and needs, it is difficult to predict how long a battery charge lasts. There are two main factors: Charging the battery When you find that the remaining battery power is low, charge your battery or replace the battery with a charged battery. If an ac outlet is convenient, connect the computer to ac power. The battery is fully charged in about four to eight hours. Your computer comes with a built-in wireless network card to help you establish wireless connections and monitor the connection status. SECTION: Chapter 4. Accessibility, ergonomic, and maintenance information (Pages 65-71)

TOPICS: accessibility features, ergonomic guidelines, maintenance procedures, keyboard shortcuts, screen customization, assistive technologies, device cleaning, password security

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- Chapter 4 covers accessibility, ergonomic, and maintenance information (Page 65)
- Lenovo supports users with hearing, vision, and mobility limitations through various features (Page 65)
- The Ease of Access Center can be opened using Windows logo key + U or accessed via Control Panel → Category view → Click Ease of Access → Ease of Access Center (Page 65)
- Keyboard shortcuts include: Windows logo key + U (Open Ease of Access Center), Right Shift for eight seconds (Filter Keys), Shift five times (Sticky Keys), Num Lock for five seconds (Toggle Keys), Left Alt+Left Shift+Num Lock (Mouse Keys), Left Alt+Left Shift+PrtScn (High Contrast) (Page 65)
- Tools in the Ease of Access Center include Magnifier (enlarges screen), Narrator (reads screen content aloud), and On-Screen Keyboard (Page 65)
- On-Screen Keyboard allows typing using a mouse or touch screen (Page 66)
- High Contrast mode enhances text and image visibility (Page 66)
- Speech Recognition enables voice-controlled computing, including starting programs, opening menus, clicking objects, dictating text, and sending emails (Page 66)
- Instructions for Speech Recognition: Go to Control Panel → Ease of Access → Speech Recognition (Page 66)
- Instructions for adjusting screen resolution: Right-click desktop → Display settings → Display (Page 66)
- Setting a resolution too low might prevent some items from fitting on the screen (Page 66)
- Users can change item size temporarily using the Magnifier tool or permanently via Display settings (Page 67)
- To change text size on a Web page, press and hold Ctrl while pressing the plus-sign (+) or minus-sign (-) key (Page 67)
- If the mouse has a wheel, users can scroll it while holding Ctrl to change item size (Page 67)
- Industry-standard connectors enable connection of assistive devices (Page 67)
- Lenovo provides electronic documentation in accessible formats such as properly tagged PDF files or HTML files (Page 67)
- Each image in the documentation includes adequate alternative text for visually impaired users (Page 67)
- Good ergonomic practice is important to avoid discomfort and maximize performance (Page 67)
- Adapting to light sources, active seating, and hardware placement can improve comfort and performance (Page 67)
- Recommended viewing distance for the display is 510 mm to 760 mm (20 inches to 30 inches) (Page 68)
- The computer should not be opened beyond 180 degrees to prevent hinge damage (Page 68)
- The computer should be kept away from magnets, activated cellular phones, electrical appliances, or speakers (more than 13 cm or 5 inches) (Page 68)
- The computer should not be subjected to extreme temperatures (below 5°C/41°F or above 35°C/95°F) (Page 68)
- ThinkPad notebook screens are designed to meet the highest standards for clear, crisp images and are easy on the eyes (Page 68)
- Do not turn the computer over when the AC power adapter is plugged in (Page 69)
- Remove media, turn off devices, and disconnect cords before moving the computer (Page 69)
- Hold the computer by the bottom when picking it up; do not pick it up by the display (Page 69)
- Only an authorized ThinkPad repair technician should disassemble and repair the computer (Page 69)
- Use a lint-free cloth dampened in mild soap and water to clean the computer cover (Page 69)
- Wipe keyboard keys one by one to avoid damage from the cloth hooking onto adjacent keys (Page 69)
- Use a camera blower with a brush or cool air from a hair dryer to remove crumbs and dust from beneath the keys (Page 69)
- Scratches, oil, dust, chemicals, and ultraviolet light can affect screen performance (Page 69)
- Clean the screen with a dry, soft lint-free cloth; if a stain remains, moisten a cloth with water or eyeglass cleaner but do not apply liquids directly (Page 69)
- Ensure the screen is dry before closing it (Page 69)
- The chapter's purpose is to provide information on protecting a computer from unauthorized use (Page 71)
- Passwords are used to prevent unauthorized access; a prompt appears on startup requiring the correct password (Page 71)
- If a Windows password is set, it is prompted upon resuming from sleep mode (Page 71)
- A power-on password is required to start the computer (Page 71)
- The supervisor password protects the ThinkPad Setup program, prevents unauthorized changes, and can override the power-on password (Page 71)
- A hard disk password prevents unauthorized access to data on the hard disk drive (Page 71)
- Two types of hard disk passwords exist, with "User hard disk password" being listed (Page 71)

pages.ocr_text: Customizable item size You can make the items on your screen easier to read by changing the item size. - Change the size of all the items on your screen. - Change the size of the items on a Web page. Press and hold Ctrl, and then press the plus-sign key (+) to enlarge or the minus-sign key (-) to reduce the text size. - Change the size of the items on the desktop or a window. Note: This function might not work on some windows. If your mouse has a wheel, press and hold Ctrl, and then scroll the wheel to change the item size. Industry-standard connectors Your computer provides industry-standard connectors that enable you to connect assistive devices. Documentation in accessible formats Lenovo provides electronic documentation in accessible formats, such as properly tagged PDF files or HyperText Markup Language (HTML) files. Lenovo electronic documentation is developed to ensure that visually impaired users can read the documentation through a screen reader. Each image in the documentation also includes adequate alternative text so that visually impaired users can understand the image when they use a screen reader. Ergonomic information Good ergonomic practice is important to get the most from your personal computer and to avoid discomfort. Arrange your workplace and the equipment you use to suit your individual needs and the kind of work that you perform. In addition, use healthy work habits to maximize your performance and comfort when using your computer. Working in the virtual office might mean adapting to frequent changes in your environment. Adapting to the surrounding light sources, active seating, and the placement of your computer hardware, can help you improve your performance and achieve greater comfort. This example shows someone in a conventional setting. Even when not in such a setting, you can follow many of these tips. Develop good habits, and they will serve you well.

You can make the items on your screen easier to read by changing the item size.

- Change the size of the items on a Web page.

pages.ocr_text: Cleaning your computer It is a good practice to clean your computer periodically to protect the surfaces and ensure trouble-free operation. Cleaning the computer cover: Wipe it with a lint-free cloth dampened in mild soap and water. Avoid applying liquids directly to the cover. Cleaning the keyboard: Wipe the keys one by one with a lint-free cloth dampened in mild soap and water. If you wipe several keys at a time, the cloth might hook onto an adjacent key and possibly damage it. Avoid spraying cleaner directly onto the keyboard. To remove any crumbs or dust from beneath the keys, you can use a camera blower with a brush or use cool air from a hair dryer. Cleaning the computer screen: Scratches, oil, dust, chemicals, and ultraviolet light can affect the performance of your computer screen. Use a dry, soft lint-free cloth to wipe the screen gently. If you see a scratchlike mark on your screen, it might be a stain. Wipe or dust the stain gently with a soft, dry cloth. If the stain remains, moisten a soft, lint-free cloth with water or eyeglass cleaner, but do not apply liquids directly to your computer screen. Ensure that the computer screen is dry before closing it.

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- The chapter's purpose is to provide information on protecting a computer from unauthorized use (Page 71)
- Passwords are used to prevent unauthorized access; a prompt appears on startup requiring the correct password (Page 71)
- If a Windows password is set, it is prompted upon resuming from sleep mode (Page 71)
- A power-on password is required to start the computer (Page 71)
- The supervisor password protects the ThinkPad Setup program, prevents unauthorized changes, and can override the power-on password (Page 71)
- A hard disk password prevents unauthorized access to data on the hard disk drive (Page 71)
- Two types of hard disk passwords exist, with "User hard disk password" being listed (Page 71)
- A user hard disk password must be entered to access files if no master password is set (Page 72)
- The master hard disk password is set by a system administrator and acts as a master key (Page 72)
- Only the administrator can remove the user hard disk password when a master password is set (Page 72)
- To type a master hard disk password, press F1; to return to the user password prompt, press F1 again (Page 72)
- Tips include setting a minimum password length and recording passwords in a safe place (Page 72)
- If passwords are forgotten, the computer must be taken to a Lenovo reseller or marketing representative for service (Page 72)
- eDrive storage drives and TCG Opal-compliant drives provide self-encryption (Page 72)
- Passwords cannot be set if TCG Opal management software is installed and activated (Page 72)
- Passwords are not available if an eDrive is installed in a Windows 10 preinstalled system (Page 72)
- Instructions for setting, changing, or removing a password involve restarting the computer, pressing F1, selecting Security → Password, and choosing the password type (Page 72)
- To enhance security, set a power-on password and a hard disk password (Page 73)
- Use UEFI BIOS and the Trusted Platform Module (TPM) management feature for reliable security (Page 73)
- Windows BitLocker Drive Encryption protects the operating system and data, even if the computer is lost or stolen (Page 73)
- A compatible TPM is defined as a V2.0 TPM (Page 73)
- For more information, search for "Microsoft Windows BitLocker Drive Encryption Step-by-Step Guide" on the Microsoft Web site (Page 73)
- Disk Encryption hard disk drive and Encryption solid-state drive use a hardware encryption chip to protect against security attacks (Page 73)
- Set a hard disk password for efficient use of the encryption feature (Page 73)
- The security chip can protect data, strengthen access controls, and secure communications (Page 73)
- Instructions are provided for setting an item on the Security Chip submenu (Page 73)
- The security chip configuration requires pressing F1 at the logo screen, navigating to Security → Security Chip, and saving changes with F10 (Page 74)
- The supervisor password must be set in ThinkPad Setup before any security chip settings can be changed (Page 74)
- Fingerprint authentication can replace Windows, power-on, and hard disk passwords (Page 74)
- To enroll fingerprints, users should open Settings → Accounts → Sign-in options and follow on-screen instructions (Page 74)
- For scanning, users should tap the fingerprint reader with the top joint of their finger and hold it for one or two seconds with slight pressure (Page 74)
- To associate fingerprints, turn off the computer, scan your finger, and enter the power-on and/or hard disk password (Page 75)
- If you forget your power-on password, you must take the computer to a Lenovo-authorized servicer or marketing representative to have it canceled (Page 75)
- If you forget your hard disk password, Lenovo cannot reset it or recover data; the storage drive must be replaced at a Lenovo-authorized servicer (Page 75)
- The fingerprint reader indicator shows Off (not ready), White (ready), or Amber blinking (cannot authenticate) (Page 75)
- Actions that can damage the reader include scratching with a hard object, scraping with a fingernail, or touching with a dirty finger (Page 75)
- Fingerprint registration may fail if the finger is wrinkled, rough, dry, injured, stained, wet, or not previously enrolled (Page 76)
- To improve fingerprint authentication, clean or wipe hands and enroll a different finger (Page 76)
- Standard data deletion methods (Recycle Bin, formatting) do not permanently delete data; special software can recover it (Page 76)
- Secure data deletion requires physical destruction (hammer, magnet) or specialized software/services (Page 76)
- Lenovo's Drive Erase Utility is available for resetting cryptographic keys and erasing solid-state drives (Page 76)
- Firewalls protect against internet security threats, unauthorized access, intrusions, and attacks (Page 76)
- For firewall usage, see the help system that comes with the program (Page 77)
- Lenovo provides a full version of antivirus software with a free 30-day subscription (Page 77)
- After 30 days, you must renew the license to continue receiving antivirus software updates (Page 77)
- For more information about your antivirus software, see the help system of your antivirus software (Page 77)
- The chapter title is "Chapter 6. Advanced configuration." (Page 79)
- The section is titled "Installing the Windows 10 operating system." (Page 79)
- Step 1 requires setting the security chip to TPM 2.0, with reference to page 55 (Page 79)
- Step 2 involves starting the ThinkPad Setup program and selecting Config → Storage → Controller Mode, ensuring RST mode is selected (Page 79)
- Step 6 requires selecting the drive containing the installation program, such as a USB HDD (Page 79)
- A note warns against changing the initial UEFI/Legacy Boot setting in the ThinkPad Setup program after installation (Page 79)
- For Intel Optane support, users must download and install the Intel Rapid Storage Technology (IRST) Console from https://support.lenovo.com (Page 79)

pages.ocr_text: Hard disk security To protect the computer from unauthorized security attacks, refer to the following tips to enhance security: Using Windows BitLocker Drive Encryption To help protect your computer against unauthorized access, use the drive encryption software, such as Windows BitLocker Drive Encryption. Windows BitLocker Drive Encryption (referred to as BitLocker) is an integral security feature of some editions of the Windows operating system. It can help you protect the operating system and data stored on your computer, even if your computer is lost or stolen. BitLocker can encrypt all user and system files, including the swap and hibernation files. BitLocker uses the TPM to provide enhanced protection for your data and to ensure early boot component integrity. A compatible TPM is defined as a V2.0 TPM. To check the BitLocker status, go to Control Panel, view Control Panel by Category, and click System and Security  $\rightarrow$  BitLocker Drive Encryption. For more information, see the help system of the Windows operating system, or search for "Microsoft Windows BitLocker Drive Encryption Step-by-Step Guide" on the Microsoft Web site. Disk Encryption hard disk drive and Encryption solid-state drive Some models contain the Disk Encryption hard disk drive, Encryption solid-state drive, or Encryption hybrid drive. This encryption technology helps to protect your computer against security attacks on media, NAND flash, or device controllers by use of a hardware encryption chip. For the efficient use of the encryption feature, set a hard disk password for the internal storage drive. Setting the security chip Strict security requirements are imposed on network client computers that transfer confidential information electronically. pages.ocr_text: If your finger has any of the following conditions, you might not be able to register or authenticate it: To improve the situation, try the following: Deleting data from your storage drive Some of the data stored on the storage drive might be sensitive. Handing your computer over to someone else without deleting the installed software, such as operating systems and programs, might even violate the license agreements. Be sure to delete data stored on the storage drive before you dispose of, sell, or hand over your computer. You can use the following methods to delete data from the storage drive: These operations, however, only change the file location of the data; they do not delete the data itself. The data is still there, even though it seems to be lost. Thus, it is sometimes possible to read the data by use of special software for data recovery. There is a risk that people of bad faith might read and misuse the critical data on storage drives for unexpected purposes. To prevent leakage of data, it is important that you delete all the data from the hard disk drive when you dispose of, sell, or hand over your computer. You can destroy the data physically by smashing the hard disk drive with a hammer, or magnetically by means of strong magnetic power, thus making the data unreadable. But it is recommended that you use the software (payware) or service (pay service) developed for that purpose. The process might take several hours. For disposing of data on the solid-state drive, Lenovo provides the Drive Erase Utility for Resetting the Cryptographic Key and Erasing the Solid State Drive tool. Some computers might support a Disk Encryption hard disk drive or Encryption solid-state drive and have such a drive installed. You can logically dispose of all the data on the drive in a short time by erasing the cryptographic key. The data encrypted with the old key is not physically erased but remains on the drive; however, it cannot be decrypted without the old key. This feature is also available with the Drive Erase Utility for Resetting the Cryptographic Key and Erasing the Solid State Drive tool. Using firewalls If your system is preinstalled with a firewall program, it protects against computer Internet security threats, unauthorized access, intrusions, and Internet attacks. It also protects your privacy.

Each hardware component on your computer has its own specific driver. If you add a component, the operating system must be instructed on how to operate that piece of hardware. After you install the driver, the operating system can recognize the hardware component and understand how to use it. Note: Because drivers are programs, like any other file on your computer, they are susceptible to corruption and might not perform properly if corruption occurs. It is not always necessary to download the latest drivers. However, you should download the latest driver for a component when you notice poor performance from that component or when you added a component. This action might eliminate the driver as the potential cause of a problem. This page (Page 67) details advanced configuration settings for a ThinkPad computer, organized into sections for keyboard functions, display options, and power management. It describes several BIOS-level settings including the Fn key swap function, Fn Sticky key, F1-F12 primary function mode, boot display device selection, shared display priority between HDMI and USB Type-C, total graphics memory allocation (256 MB or 512 MB), boot time extension (up to 10 seconds), and Intel SpeedStep® technology. - Boot Time Extension can be set from Disabled to 10 seconds to allow monitors time to initialize.

This page (Page 71) details advanced security configuration options for a computer system, primarily focusing on password and fingerprint authentication settings. It lists several BIOS-level password features such as "Password at Unattended Boot," "Password at Restart," and "Power-On Password," each with descriptions of their function and available values (Disabled/Enabled). The page also covers the "Set Minimum Length" option, which allows users to specify a minimum password length between 4 and 12 characters. Additionally, it describes fingerprint authentication settings, including "Predesktop Authentication," "Reader Priority," and "Security Mode," which determines whether a power-on or supervisor password can be used if fingerprint authentication fails. Cross-references are made to the "Passwords introduction" section on page 53 for further information.

- "Fingerprint Predesktop Authentication" enables or disables fingerprint login before the OS loads.
- "Reader Priority" can be set to External → Internal or Internal Only.

pages.summary:
This page (Page 72) from the T480 User Guide details various security and firmware update settings within a system's UEFI BIOS. It outlines options for fingerprint authentication, security chip configuration (including TPM 2.0), Intel TXT, and UEFI BIOS updates. Key features include the ability to reset fingerprint data, enable or disable the security chip, log BIOS changes via SMBIOS reporting, clear encryption keys, and control who can update the firmware, with specific options for end-user flashing and secure rollback prevention.

**Text Evidence:**
- The "Reset Fingerprint Data" option erases all stored fingerprint data and resets settings to factory defaults.
- The "Security Chip Type" is specified as TPM 2.0.
- The "Security Chip" can be set to Enabled or Disabled.
- "SMBIOS Reporting" logs UEFI BIOS data changes in PCR1 when enabled.
- The "Clear Security Chip" function removes encryption keys, making encrypted data inaccessible.
- The "Intel (R) TXT Feature" can be enabled or disabled.
- "Flash BIOS Updating by End-Users" allows all users to update the BIOS if enabled; otherwise, a supervisor password is required.
- "Secure Rollback Prevention" prevents flashing to earlier BIOS versions when enabled.
- "Windows UEFI Firmware Update" enables or disables the Windows feature for updating firmware.

General tips for preventing problems This topic provides the following tips to help you prevent computing problems: - Empty your recycle bin on a regular basis. - Use a disk defragment tool regularly on your storage drive to improve data seek and read times. - To free up disk space, uninstall unused programs. You also might want to look for program duplication or overlapping versions. - Clean out your Inbox, Sent, and Trash folders from your e-mail client program. - Back up your data at least once a week. If critical data is present, it is a good idea to back up the data daily. Lenovo has many backup options available for your computer. - Schedule system restore operations to take a system snapshot periodically. For information about system restore, see Chapter 8 "Recovery information" on page 97. - Go to https://support.lenovo.com to download and install updates for the device drivers and UEFI BIOS when needed. - Keep up to date for device drivers on other non-Lenovo hardware. Before updating device drivers, read the device driver information release notes for compatibility or known issues. - Keep a log book. Entries might include major hardware or software changes, driver updates, minor issues you have experienced, and how you resolved the minor issues. - If you ever need to run a recovery on your computer to return the preinstalled contents onto the machine, the following tips might help along the way: Diagnosing problems Many computer problems can be solved without outside assistance. If you experience a problem with your computer, the first place to start is the troubleshooting information in your computer documentation. If you suspect a software problem, see the documentation, includingREADME files and help information systems, that come with the operating system or program. ThinkPad notebook computers come with a set of diagnostic programs that you can use to help you identify hardware problems. Note: If you are unable to isolate and repair the problem yourself after running Lenovo Vantage, save and print the log files created by the program. You need the log files when you speak to a Lenovo technical support representative. Lenovo Vantage supports the hardware scan function. elements.text: Chapter 7. Troubleshooting computer problems
This chapter provides information about what to do if you experience a problem with your computer.
General tips for preventing problems
This topic provides the following tips to help you prevent computing problems:
- Empty your recycle bin on a regular basis.
- Use a disk defragment tool regularly on your storage drive to improve data seek and read times.
- To free up disk space, uninstall unused programs. You also might want to look for program duplication or overlapping versions.
- Clean out your Inbox, Sent, and Trash folders from your e-mail client program.
- Back up your data at least once a week. If critical data is present, it is a good idea to back up the data daily. Lenovo has many backup options available for your computer.
- Schedule system restore operations to take a system snapshot periodically. For information about system restore, see Chapter 8 "Recovery information" on page 97.
- Go to https://support.lenovo.com to download and install updates for the device drivers and UEFI BIOS when needed.
- Keep up to date for device drivers on other non-Lenovo hardware. Before updating device drivers, read the device driver information release notes for compatibility or known issues.
- Keep a log book. Entries might include major hardware or software changes, driver updates, minor issues you have experienced, and how you resolved the minor issues.
- If you ever need to run a recovery on your computer to return the preinstalled contents onto the machine, the following tips might help along the way:
Diagnosing problems

Many computer problems can be solved without outside assistance. If you experience a problem with your computer, the first place to start is the troubleshooting information in your computer documentation. If you suspect a software problem, see the documentation, includingREADME files and help information systems, that come with the operating system or program. ThinkPad notebook computers come with a set of diagnostic programs that you can use to help you identify hardware problems.

Note: If you are unable to isolate and repair the problem yourself after running Lenovo Vantage, save and print the log files created by the program. You need the log files when you speak to a Lenovo technical support representative.

Lenovo Vantage supports the hardware scan function. It combines diagnostic tests, system information collection, security status, and support information, along with hints and tips for optimal system performance. To run Lenovo Vantage, see "Accessing Lenovo programs" on page 14.
Copyright Lenovo 2018

- For recovery, remove external devices, ensure the battery is charged and AC power is connected, access ThinkPad Setup, restart the computer, and do not remove the disc until prompted (Page 97)
- Lenovo Vantage supports hardware scan function, combining diagnostic tests, system information collection, security status, and support information (Page 97)
- Users can download device drivers and updates from https://support.lenovo.com (Page 98)
- Liquid spilled on a keyboard can cause short circuits; immediate action includes unplugging the AC adapter and turning off the computer (Page 99)
- Error message 0177 indicates an incorrect checksum of the supervisor password in EEPROM, requiring system board replacement (Page 99)
- Error message 0183 indicates an incorrect checksum of Security Settings in EFI Variable, requiring entry into ThinkPad Setup (Page 99)
- Error message 0190 indicates the computer turned off due to low battery power, requiring connection to an AC power adapter (Page 99)
- Error message 1802 indicates an unauthorized network card is plugged in, requiring it to be removed (Page 99)
- Error message 1820 indicates more than one external fingerprint reader is attached, which is not supported (Page 99)
- Error message 2100 indicates a detection error on HDD0 (Main HDD), with a solution to have the hard disk drive serviced (Page 100)
- Error message 2101 indicates a detection error on SSD1 (M.2), with a solution to have the M.2 solid-state drive serviced (Page 100)
- Error message 2200 indicates invalid Machine Type and Serial Number, requiring the computer to be serviced (Page 100)
- Error message 2201 indicates invalid Machine UUID, requiring the computer to be serviced (Page 100)
- The "Error: The non-volatile system UEFI variable storage is nearly full" occurs when there is insufficient space after POST, and the solution involves pressing F1 to enter ThinkPad Setup and confirming cleanup (Page 100)
- Lenovo SmartBeep technology allows users to decode beep errors with their smartphone (Page 100)
- Error code 0001 indicates a reset error; solution involves removing all power resources (Page 101)
- Error code 0281 indicates a general embedded controller error; solution involves reinstalling or replacing components (Page 101)
- Error code 0282 indicates a memory module error; solution involves replacing the memory module (Page 101)
- Error code 0287 indicates a discrete graphics error; solution involves reinstalling or replacing the discrete graphics card or system board (service provider only) (Page 102)
- Error code 0288 indicates a computer display error; solution involves reconnecting the display cable or replacing the system board (service provider only) (Page 102)
- Memory module problem solution includes verifying installation, checking BIOS, installing the latest UEFI BIOS, verifying memory configuration, and running diagnostic programs (Page 102)
- Ethernet problem solution requires checking cable installation (maximum distance 100 m / 328 ft), using the correct device driver, updating drivers via Device Manager, and ensuring matching duplex settings (Page 102)
- A Gigabit Ethernet model may fail to connect at 1000 Mbps and instead connect at 100 Mbps; solution includes using Category 5 wiring and connecting to a 1000 BASE-T hub/switch (Page 103)
- The Wake on LAN feature requires enabling in ThinkPad Setup and checking with the LAN administrator (Page 103)
- An unauthorized WAN card is not supported and must be removed (Page 103)
- Simultaneous searching by multiple Bluetooth-enabled devices is not allowed during connection (Page 103)
- Sound device conflicts can be resolved by setting default audio profiles in Control Panel (Page 104)
- Pointer drift on TrackPoint devices is normal during startup, resume, or temperature changes (Page 104)
- Keyboard problems may require removing external numeric keypads and checking device drivers (Page 104)
- Problem: My screen keeps blanking when I do not want it to. Solution: Go to Control Panel → Hardware and Sound → Power Options → High performance (Page 105)
- Problem: When I turn on the computer, nothing is displayed and the computer does not beep. Solution: Ensure battery, power adapter, and power cord are correctly connected; check brightness level; enter power-on password if set (Page 105)
- Problem: Only a white cursor is displayed on a blank screen. Solution: If partition software was used, examine and recover the partition or use recovery solutions to restore factory default state (see Chapter 8, page 97) (Page 105)
- Problem: The screen goes blank while the computer is on. Solution: Disable screen saver or power management by touching the TrackPoint/trackpad or pressing a key, or press the power button to resume from sleep/hibernation (Page 105)
- If the Fn and function keys tab is not displayed, download and install the ThinkPad Hotkey Features program from Lenovo Support (see "Installing device drivers" on page 62) (Page 105)
- For an unreadable screen, ensure the display driver is installed correctly, resolution and color quality are set properly, and the monitor type is correct (Page 106)
- To update the driver, click Browse my computer for driver software, let me pick from a list, and clear the Show compatible hardware check box (Page 106)
- Incorrect characters indicate improper OS and program installation; if unresolved, service the computer (Page 106)
- A computer that won't turn off can be forced off by pressing and holding the power button for four seconds or more (Page 106)
- Missing, discolored, or bright dots are an intrinsic characteristic of TFT technology, caused by thin-film transistors (TFTs) (Page 106)
- Problem: The external monitor is blank. Solution: Press the display-mode switching key and select the monitor you want (Page 107)
- Problem: I cannot set a higher resolution than the present one on my external monitor. Solution: Ensure that the monitor information is correct. If necessary, update the monitor driver (Page 107)
- Problem: The screen is unreadable or distorted. Solution: Ensure that the monitor information is correct and the appropriate monitor type is selected. Update the monitor driver if needed (Page 107)
- Problem: The Extend desktop function does not work. Solution: Enable the Extend desktop function. See "Using an external display" on page 36 (Page 107)
- Problem: Display switching does not work. Solution: Disable the Extend desktop function and change the display output location (Page 107)
- Screen position shifts left or right on external monitors at high resolutions; external monitors may need manual adjustment via their setup menu (Page 108)
- Audio problems include Wave/MIDI sound not playing properly (Page 108)
- Microphone recordings can be made louder by enabling Microphone Boost (Page 108)
- Volume sliders may be grayed out due to hardware limitations (Page 108)
- Volume sliders can change position when certain audio programs are used (e.g., Windows Media Player) (Page 108)
- The balance slider cannot completely mute either channel (Page 108)
- There is no volume control for MIDI sound in the Volume Mixer window (Page 108)
- Sound cannot be turned off even when the Master volume is set to minimum (Page 108)
- To turn off sound completely, select "Mute Speaker/HP" in the Master volume control (Page 109)
- When headphones are connected, audio streaming is automatically redirected to them; to use speakers again, set them as the default device (Page 109)
- To switch audio devices, go to Control Panel > Hardware and Sound > Sound > Playback tab > Set Default (Page 109)
- For a dirty fingerprint reader, gently clean it with a dry, soft, lint-free cloth (Page 109)
- If a battery cannot be fully charged in 24 hours, use a new battery (Page 109)
- The computer shuts down before the battery status icon shows it's empty, or operates after it shows it's empty, both requiring discharge and recharge (Page 109)
- Problem: Short battery operating time; Solution: Discharge and recharge the battery, or use a new one (Page 110)
- Problem: Computer does not operate with a fully charged battery; Solution: Turn off the computer for one minute to reset the surge protector (Page 110)
- Problem: Battery cannot get charged due to heat; Solution: Remove the battery, let it cool to room temperature, then reinstall and recharge (Page 110)
- Problem: AC power adapter icon not displayed; Solution: Check connection, disconnect and reconnect components, or have it serviced (Page 110)
- Problem: No power at all; Solution: Check the power button, power connections, and power source (Page 110)
- Problem: System does not respond; Solution: Press and hold the power button for four seconds or more, or remove the AC adapter and battery (Page 110)

- If the system still does not respond, remove the AC power adapter and reset the system by inserting a needle or paper clip into the emergency-reset hole (Page 111)
- For boot problems, users should follow corrective actions for POST error messages or search for solutions online at support.lenovo.com and support.microsoft.com (Page 111)

- To reset the computer, press and hold the power button for four seconds or more (Page 112)
- If the computer does not enter sleep or hibernation mode, check if any option has been selected to disable it (Page 112)

This chapter provides information about what to do if you experience a problem with your computer.
General tips for preventing problems
This topic provides the following tips to help you prevent computing problems:
- Empty your recycle bin on a regular basis.
- Use a disk defragment tool regularly on your storage drive to improve data seek and read times.
- To free up disk space, uninstall unused programs. You also might want to look for program duplication or overlapping versions.
- Clean out your Inbox, Sent, and Trash folders from your e-mail client program.
- Back up your data at least once a week. If critical data is present, it is a good idea to back up the data daily. Lenovo has many backup options available for your computer.
- Schedule system restore operations to take a system snapshot periodically. For information about system restore, see Chapter 8 "Recovery information" on page 97.
- Go to https://support.lenovo.com to download and install updates for the device drivers and UEFI BIOS when needed.
- Keep up to date for device drivers on other non-Lenovo hardware. Before updating device drivers, read the device driver information release notes for compatibility or known issues.
- Keep a log book. Entries might include major hardware or software changes, driver updates, minor issues you have experienced, and how you resolved the minor issues.
- If you ever need to run a recovery on your computer to return the preinstalled contents onto the machine, the following tips might help along the way:
Diagnosing problems

Many computer problems can be solved without outside assistance. If you experience a problem with your computer, the first place to start is the troubleshooting information in your computer documentation. If you suspect a software problem, see the documentation, includingREADME files and help information systems, that come with the operating system or program. ThinkPad notebook computers come with a set of diagnostic programs that you can use to help you identify hardware problems.

Note: If you are unable to isolate and repair the problem yourself after running Lenovo Vantage, save and print the log files created by the program. You need the log files when you speak to a Lenovo technical support representative.

Lenovo Vantage supports the hardware scan function. It combines diagnostic tests, system information collection, security status, and support information, along with hints and tips for optimal system performance. To run Lenovo Vantage, see "Accessing Lenovo programs" on page 14.

It details steps to resolve an unreadable or distorted screen by checking display settings, drivers, and monitor type, including a 12-step process for updating drivers. The page also addresses problems with incorrect characters on the screen, a computer that won't turn off completely, and persistent dots on the display, explaining that the latter is a normal characteristic of TFT technology due to thin-film transistors.

**Text Evidence:**
- For an unreadable screen, ensure the display driver is installed correctly, resolution and color quality are set properly, and the monitor type is correct.
- To check settings, right-click desktop, click Display settings → Display, then select external monitor and set Resolution.
- If more than two monitor types are displayed, select Generic PnP Monitor or Generic Non-PnP Monitor.
- To update the driver, click Browse my computer for driver software, let me pick from a list, and clear the Show compatible hardware check box.
- Incorrect characters indicate improper OS and program installation; if unresolved, service the computer.
- A computer that won't turn off can be forced off by pressing and holding the power button for four seconds or more.
- Missing, discolored, or bright dots are an intrinsic characteristic of TFT technology, caused by thin-film transistors (TFTs).

pages.summary:
This page from the T480 User Guide (page 100) provides critical instructions for preventing static electricity damage when handling computer components. It details precautions such as limiting movement, handling parts by edges, and grounding oneself by touching metal surfaces before installing static-sensitive options or Customer Replaceable Units (CRUs). The page also includes step-by-step procedures for disabling Fast Startup and the built-in battery, with specific actions like navigating the Control Panel and using the ThinkPad Setup. - Static electricity can seriously damage computer components and options.
- Do not open static-protective packages until instructed to install the part.
- Precautions include limiting movement, handling components by edges, and grounding by touching metal surfaces for at least two seconds.

- Before replacing the removable battery, read "Important safety information" on page v.

Downloading system updates Downloading updated software might resolve problems you experience with your computer. To download updated software, go to the following Web site and follow the instructions on the screen: https://support.lenovo.com Recording information Before you talk to a Lenovo representative, record the following important information about your computer. Recording problem symptoms and details Collect the answers to the following questions before you call for help. Then, you are able to get help as quickly as possible. Recording system information The serial number label is on the bottom of your computer. Record the machine type and the serial number. Getting help and service If you need help, service, technical assistance, or more information about Lenovo products, you will find a wide variety of sources available from Lenovo to assist you. Information about your computer and preinstalled software, if any, is available in the documentation that comes with your computer or on the Lenovo Support Web site at https://support.lenovo.com. The documentation includes printed books, online books, readme files, and help files.

elements.text: Chapter 10. Getting support
This chapter provides information about getting help and support from Lenovo.
Before you contact Lenovo
Often, you can solve your computer problems by referring to the information in the explanations of error codes, running diagnostic programs, or by consulting the Lenovo Support Web site.
Registering your computer
Register your computer with Lenovo. For more information, see "Registering your computer" on page 17.
Downloading system updates
Downloading updated software might resolve problems you experience with your computer.
To download updated software, go to the following Web site and follow the instructions on the screen:
https://support.lenovo.com
Recording information
Before you talk to a Lenovo representative, record the following important information about your computer.
Recording problem symptoms and details
Collect the answers to the following questions before you call for help. Then, you are able to get help as quickly as possible.
Recording system information
The serial number label is on the bottom of your computer. Record the machine type and the serial number.
Getting help and service
If you need help, service, technical assistance, or more information about Lenovo products, you will find a wide variety of sources available from Lenovo to assist you.

Information about your computer and preinstalled software, if any, is available in the documentation that comes with your computer or on the Lenovo Support Web site at https://support.lenovo.com. The documentation includes printed books, online books, readme files, and help files.
Copyright Lenovo 2018

pages.ocr_text: Appendix C. WEEE and recycling statements of countries and regions This chapter provides environmental information about Lenovo products. General recycling information Lenovo encourages owners of information technology (IT) equipment to responsibly recycle their equipment when it is no longer needed. Lenovo offers a variety of programs and services to assist equipment owners in recycling their IT products. For information about recycling Lenovo products, go to: https://www.lenovo.com/recycling The latest environmental information about our products is available at: https://www.lenovo.com/ecodeclaration Important WEEE information The WEEE marking on Lenovo products applies to countries with WEEE and e-waste regulations (for example, the European WEEE Directive, India E-Waste Management Rules). Appliances are labeled in accordance with local regulations concerning waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE). These regulations determine the framework for the return and recycling of used appliances as applicable within each geography. This label is applied to various products to indicate that the product is not to be thrown away, but rather put in the established collection systems for reclaiming these end of life products. Users of electrical and electronic equipment (EEE) with the WEEE marking must not dispose of end of life EEE as unsorted municipal waste, but use the collection framework available to them for the return, recycle, and recovery of WEEE and to minimize any potential effects of EEE on the environment and human health due to the presence of hazardous substances. Lenovo electrical and electronic equipment (EEE) may contain parts and components, which at end-of-life might qualify as hazardous waste. EEE and waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) can be delivered free of charge to the place of sale or any distributor that sells electrical and electronic equipment of the same nature and function as the used EEE or WEEE. For additional WEEE information, go to: https://www.lenovo.com/recycling

SECTION: Appendix D. Restriction of Hazardous Substances (RoHS) Directive of countries and regions. (Pages 159-163)

TOPICS: RoHS compliance, country-specific regulations, harmful substances, environmental use period, power management

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- The Lenovo product meets the requirements of Directive 2011/65/EU (RoHS recast or RoHS 2) for the European Union. (Page 159)
- The product complies with the Republic of Turkey Directive on WEEE. (Page 159)
- The product is compliant with Ukrainian normative acts regarding hazardous substances. (Page 159)
- The product is RoHS compliant as per India's E-Waste (Management) Rules. (Page 159)
- Information for China RoHS applies to products manufactured on or after January 1, 2015. (Page 159)
- The latest environmental information is available at https://www.lenovo.com/ecodeclaration. (Page 159)
- More information on worldwide compliance can be found at https://www.lenovo.com/rohs-communication. (Page 159)
- The table is based on SJ/T 11364 regulations. (Page 160)
- 'O' means the substance's content is below the GB/T 26572 standard limit. (Page 160)
- 'X' means the substance's content exceeds the GB/T 26572 standard limit in at least one homogeneous material. (Page 160)
- Components with 'X' cannot have their harmful substances replaced due to global technical development levels. (Page 160)
- The EPuP symbol is used on electronic products sold in China, with the number inside representing the normal environmental use period. (Page 160)
- The document is titled "Taiwan RoHS" and is from Appendix D. (Page 161)
- The table covers six restricted substances: Lead (Pb), Mercury (Hg), Cadmium (Cd), Hexavalent chromium (Cr⁶⁺), Polybrominated biphenyls (PBB), and Polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDE). (Page 161)
- The table includes notes explaining that "exceeding 0.1 wt %" or "exceeding 0.01 wt %" means the substance content exceeds the reference value, "○" means it does not exceed the value, and "-" indicates an exemption. (Page 161)
- The table applies to components such as printed circuit board assemblies, hard drives, LCD panels, keyboards, memory, power supplies, and fans. (Page 161)
- ENERGY STAR is a joint program of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the U.S. Department of Energy. (Page 163)
- Lenovo offers products with the ENERGY STAR qualified designation. (Page 163)
- Specific machine types are 20L5 and 20L6. (Page 163)
- Using ENERGY STAR qualified products can lead to financial savings and environmental protection. (Page 163)
- The default power plan turns off the display after 10 minutes and puts the computer to sleep after 30 minutes. (Page 163)
- The Wake on LAN function is enabled by default and can be disabled in the Device Manager. (Page 163)

The table indicates that lead (Pb) is present in all listed components, marked with an 'X', while all other harmful substances are absent (marked with 'O'). A note explains that 'X' signifies the substance exceeds the GB/T 26572 standard limit, and this is due to current technological limitations. The page also includes a figure illustrating the "环保使用期限" (EPuP) symbol, which is a circular icon with the number 10, indicating a 10-year normal environmental use period for products sold in China.

- The table is based on SJ/T 11364 regulations.
- 'O' means the substance's content is below the GB/T 26572 standard limit.
- 'X' means the substance's content exceeds the GB/T 26572 standard limit in at least one homogeneous material.
- Components with 'X' cannot have their harmful substances replaced due to global technical development levels.
- The EPuP symbol is used on electronic products sold in China, with the number inside representing the normal environmental use period.
